subject: mass-communication
title: What is News?
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper

Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Train timings are news. (ii) News is a report of a current event.
questions.answer: (i) False – it is information. (ii) True.

questions.q: Name the types of news by area.
questions.answer: International, national, regional and local news.

questions.q: Match: (i) Oddity (ii) Prominence (iii) Emotion (iv) Proximity with (a) the Prime Minister's visit (b) a man pulling a car by hair (c) human interest (d) nearby events.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Distinguish between hard news and soft news with examples.
questions.answer: Hard news is serious and important, e.g. India–Pakistan talks; soft news is light and human interest, e.g. a film star's wedding.

questions.q: What is meant by objectivity and fairness in news?
questions.answer: Objectivity means reporting without bias; fairness means not taking sides and giving the other party's version.

questions.q: Differentiate between news and information.
questions.answer: Information (train timings) is general; it becomes news when something new is added, such as a changed timetable.

questions.q: What is meant by currency in news?
questions.answer: News is about current events of wide interest, e.g. the Olympic Games held in India.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Discuss the importance of timeliness, proximity and impact in news value.
questions.answer: Timeliness: news must be new (previous day for a paper, every second for a news channel). Proximity: events near us matter more (bird flu in West Bengal). Impact: events affecting many people are big news (the tsunami).

questions.q: Write short notes on any two news values: proximity, timeliness, impact, controversy.
questions.answer: Timeliness: news is new and varies by medium. Impact: the wider the effect on people, the bigger the news.

questions.q: Explain the five Ws and one H of news.
questions.answer: When, Where, What, Why, Who and How; a news item that answers all six is complete.

questions.q: Explain credibility, fairness and objectivity in news.
questions.answer: Cross-check facts; stay unbiased; hear both sides; credibility is the most important virtue because readers trust a paper for it.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define news. Describe the main types of news.
questions.answer: News is a report of a current event, not known earlier and of wide interest. Types: international, national, regional, local; hard and soft; by subject such as politics, sports, economy, entertainment and crime.

questions.q: Describe the news values.
questions.answer: Timeliness, impact, proximity, controversy, prominence, currency, oddity, emotion, usefulness and educational value, each decides whether an event is newsworthy, with examples.

questions.q: Explain how news acts as a powerful tool.
questions.answer: News can be positive (voluntary service, NGO stories), negative (communal clash reports provoking tension) and developmental (fee concession for students); credibility and fairness are essential.
